realweather.cmd.snow: Snowfall set to %s%% for %s minutes (snow falls in cold biomes)
realweather.cmd.sandstorm: Sandstorm %s%% for %s minutes (deserts, badlands and savannas)
realweather.cmd.blizzard: Blizzard %s%% for %s minutes (snowy biomes; warm places get a windy downpour)
realweather.cmd.flood.depth: Floods can now be up to %s blocks deep
realweather.cmd.info:
Rain %s%%, snow %s%%, thunder %s%%, wind %s%% towards %s°, sandstorm %s%%, blizzard %s%%

realweather.configuration.title: Real Weather
realweather.config.quality.tooltip: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, ULTRA or ULTRA_3D. Lower settings draw fewer particles and clouds; LOW is best for phones and weak PCs. ULTRA_3D draws real volumetric 3D clouds (needs a strong graphics card).
death.attack.realweather.tornado: %1$s was swept away by a tornado
death.attack.realweather.tornado.player: %1$s was swept away by a tornado while fighting %2$s
realweather.cmd.tornado: A %s tornado is touching down %s blocks away
realweather.cmd.tornado.too_many: There are already too many tornadoes
realweather.cmd.tornado.damage.on: Tornadoes now tear up the ground
realweather.cmd.tornado.natural.on: Tornadoes can form in strong thunderstorms
realweather.config.tornado_quality.toolt: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or ULTRA. Separate from the rain and snow detail.
death.attack.realweather.hail.player: %1$s was battered by hail while fighting %2$s
realweather.cmd.hail.on: Hail piles up and stings again
realweather.cmd.hail.off: Hail no longer piles up or hurts
realweather.cmd.storm.2: A hailstorm (%s%%) is coming for %s minutes
realweather.cmd.storm.3: A supercell is approaching (%s%%, %s minutes) - watch the wall cloud
realweather.config.max_optimize.tooltip: Clouds, storms, tornado parts, rain, snow and puddles that are entirely off the screen are not built or drawn. What you see and hear stays exactly the same; only the work for what you can't see is saved.
realweather.config.clouds.tooltip: 3D cumulus on fair days, grey overcast in rain, and towering storm clouds with rain shafts and wall clouds. Replaces the vanilla clouds.
realweather.radar.title: Doppler Weather Radar
realweather.radar.no_signal.hint: Place a Weather Radar within %s blocks
realweather.radar.hail_here: Hail falling here: up to %s cm
realweather.radar.tornado_wind: Est. winds %s km/h, moving %s at %s km/h
realweather.radar.tds: Debris signature (TDS): tornado on the ground
realweather.radar.hail_warning: Severe hail up to %s cm, %s to the %s
item.realweather.sedan.desc: A civilian car. Light: tornadoes toss it easily.
item.realweather.pickup.desc: Chase pickup with a mobile Doppler, anemometer and probes: reads a tornado's winds and rating within 150 blocks.
item.realweather.intercept.desc: Armoured. Drives hydraulic spikes into the ground to hold on and measure a tornado from inside it.
realweather.vehicle.spikes.down: Spikes down: anchored to the ground
realweather.vehicle.spikes.stop_first: Stop the vehicle before lowering the spikes
realweather.vehicle.hud.bogged: Bogged in sand - rock back and forth
realweather.vehicle.hud.broken: Windows broken - repair with an iron ingot
realweather.vehicle.hud.keys: W/S drive  A/D steer  Space handbrake  %s wipers  %s lights  %s horn
realweather.vehicle.hud.keys_spikes: W/S drive  A/D steer  Space handbrake  %s wipers  %s lights  %s horn  %s spikes
realweather.vehicle.probe.title: In-situ wind probe
realweather.vehicle.doppler.title: Mobile Doppler
realweather.vehicle.probe.too_far: Tornado %s m away - get within %s m
realweather.vehicle.probe.deploy: Stop and lower the spikes (%s) to measure
realweather.vehicle.door_hint: Click a door to open it, click again to get in
item.realweather.suv.desc: Big three-row SUV with a V8. Heavy, but a tornado still lifts it.
item.realweather.coupe.desc: Rear-drive V8 coupe: loud start, crackling exhaust, 250 km/h.
item.realweather.sport.desc: Twin-turbo four-door: 250 km/h, pops and flames on the overrun.
realweather.cmd.graphics: Tornado graphics: %s, weather detail: %s (change with /rwgraphics tornado|weather low|medium|high|ultra|ultra_3d)
realweather.cmd.tornado.custom: A custom %s tornado, %s blocks wide (%s), is touching down %s blocks away
realweather.cmd.tsunami: A tsunami of strength %s is coming in: a wave about %s blocks high, %s blocks away
realweather.cmd.tsunami.stop: The tsunami runs out and the water drains away
realweather.cmd.tsunami.water.on: Tsunamis leave real water on the land (it drains after five minutes): on
realweather.cmd.tsunami.water.off: Tsunamis leave real water on the land: off
realweather.cmd.earthquake: An earthquake of magnitude %s: the epicentre is %s blocks away, the ground will shake for %s seconds
realweather.cmd.eclipse.total: A total solar eclipse is beginning: the moon will cover the sun completely (about %s minutes). Wear eclipse glasses to look at it!
realweather.cmd.eclipse.partial: A partial solar eclipse is beginning (about %s minutes). Wear eclipse glasses to look at it!
realweather.cmd.eclipse.night: The sun is down: an eclipse needs the sun in the sky
realweather.eclipse.eyes: Your eyes burn! Never look at the sun without eclipse glasses
item.realweather.eclipse_glasses.tip: Wear them to look at the sun during an eclipse
realweather.sky.occultation: Occultation of a planet by the moon
realweather.cmd.sky.tonight: %s will happen tonight, after dark (about %s minutes)
realweather.cmd.sky.daytime: %s has begun: it is seen at the sun, in the daytime
realweather.cmd.sky.rainbow_high: The rainbow is there: it shows whenever the sun is low enough (morning or evening). With the sun higher than 42 degrees the bow is below the horizon
realweather.cmd.eclipse.annular: An annular solar eclipse is beginning: the moon is too small to cover the sun and leaves a ring of fire (about %s minutes). Wear eclipse glasses!
realweather.cmd.eclipse.hybrid: A hybrid solar eclipse is beginning: a ring of fire that closes into totality and opens again (about %s minutes). Wear eclipse glasses!
realweather.cmd.lightning: A bolt of %s lightning struck %s blocks away
realweather.telescope.title: Telescope: what do you want to look at?
realweather.telescope.started: Telescope set for %s: follow the marker, then zoom in
realweather.telescope.hint: Zoom: mouse wheel, or hold attack (in) / use (out). Sneak to step back.
realweather.telescope.below: Below the horizon right now: wait until it rises.
realweather.target.moon.info: Craters, seas of old lava and mountains, in tonight's phase.
realweather.target.mercury.info: Small and cratered; always close to the sun, low at dusk or dawn.
realweather.target.venus.info: Wrapped in bright clouds; shows phases like the Moon. Near the sun.
realweather.target.mars.info: The red planet, with dark markings and white polar caps.
realweather.target.jupiter.info: Belts, zones and the Great Red Spot; four big moons in a line beside it.
realweather.target.saturn.info: Its rings, with the Cassini gap, and its moon Titan.
realweather.target.neptune.info: A deep blue ice giant with dark storms; very small and faint.
realweather.target.sirius.info: The brightest star of the night, with its white dwarf Sirius B.
realweather.target.betelgeuse.info: A red supergiant, boiling with huge convection cells.
realweather.target.polaris.info: The Pole Star: a yellow-white supergiant.
realweather.target.antares.info: A red supergiant with a small blue companion.
realweather.target.gj436b.info: A warm Neptune round a red dwarf, trailing a comet-like tail of hydrogen.
realweather.target.lhs1140b.info: A super-Earth in its red dwarf's habitable zone: maybe an ocean world under ice.
realweather.target.k2_18b.info: A sub-Neptune that may be a 'hycean' world: an ocean under a hydrogen sky.
realweather.target.toi700d.info: An Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of a red dwarf.
realweather.target.toi700e.info: A slightly smaller Earth-sized world, also in the habitable zone.
realweather.target.betapic_b.info: A young giant planet in the dusty disc round its star, seen edge-on.
realweather.target.hr8799b.info: The outermost of four young giants, still glowing from their birth.
realweather.target.hr8799c.info: One of four young giant planets photographed round their star.
realweather.target.hr8799d.info: One of four young giant planets photographed round their star.
realweather.target.hr8799e.info: The innermost of the four young giants.
realweather.target.psr_b1620_26b.info: A very old planet round a pulsar and a white dwarf, in the globular cluster M4.
realweather.target.sun.info: Seen through a solar filter: granulation, sunspots and prominences.
realweather.target.earth.info: Our own planet, right under your feet.
realweather.target.ceres.info: The largest body of the asteroid belt, with bright salt spots.
realweather.target.pluto.info: A dwarf planet with a bright heart of nitrogen ice, and its moon Charon.
realweather.target.haumea.info: An egg-shaped dwarf planet that spins in four hours, with a ring and two moons.
realweather.target.makemake.info: A reddish-brown icy dwarf planet beyond Pluto.
realweather.target.eris.info: A bright white dwarf planet far beyond Pluto, with its moon Dysnomia.
realweather.target.proxima_centauri.info: The nearest star to the Sun: a small red dwarf that flares.
realweather.target.alpha_centauri_a.info: A Sun-like star, going round Alpha Centauri B.
realweather.target.alpha_centauri_b.info: An orange star, the partner of Alpha Centauri A.
realweather.target.rigel_kentaurus.info: The old name of Alpha Centauri: the two stars together.
realweather.target.altair.info: A white star spinning so fast it is flattened at the poles.
realweather.target.deneb.info: A distant, enormously bright white supergiant.
realweather.target.aldebaran.info: An orange giant, the eye of the Bull.
realweather.target.arcturus.info: An old orange giant, bright in spring skies.
realweather.target.spica.info: Two hot blue stars so close they are pulled into egg shapes.
realweather.target.canopus.info: The second-brightest star of the night, a white-yellow supergiant.
realweather.target.capella.info: Two yellow giants going round each other.
realweather.target.regulus.info: A blue-white star flattened by its fast spin.
realweather.target.fomalhaut.info: A white star inside a tilted, off-centre ring of dust.
realweather.target.barnards_star.info: A small, old red dwarf, one of our nearest neighbours.
realweather.target.wolf_359.info: A faint red dwarf that keeps flaring up.
realweather.target.tau_ceti.info: A Sun-like star with a wide disc of dust.
realweather.target.epsilon_eridani.info: A young orange star with belts of dust round it.
realweather.target.uy_scuti.info: One of the largest stars known: a boiling red hypergiant.
realweather.target.vy_canis_majoris.info: A red hypergiant wrapped in the dust it throws off.
realweather.target.stephenson_2_18.info: Perhaps the largest star known, a red supergiant.
realweather.target.eta_carinae.info: A violent giant inside the two great lobes of the Homunculus nebula.
realweather.target.proxima_b.info: The nearest exoplanet: a rocky world, maybe an ocean in a shell of ice.
realweather.target.peg51b.info: The first planet found round a Sun-like star: a hot Jupiter.
realweather.target.cnc55e.info: A scorching super-Earth that may be covered in lava.
realweather.target.hd189733b.info: A deep blue hot Jupiter where it rains glass sideways.
realweather.target.hd209458b.info: 'Osiris': a hot Jupiter losing its air in a long tail.
realweather.target.wasp12b.info: A pitch-dark planet stretched into an egg and torn apart by its star.
realweather.target.wasp76b.info: An ultra-hot giant where iron rains on the night side.
realweather.target.wasp17b.info: A puffy giant twice Jupiter's size, orbiting backwards.
realweather.target.kelt9b.info: The hottest planet known, hotter than many stars.
realweather.target.kepler16b.info: A cold giant with two suns, like Tatooine.
realweather.target.kepler22b.info: Maybe an ocean world in its star's habitable zone.
realweather.target.kepler186f.info: The first Earth-sized planet found in a habitable zone.
realweather.target.kepler452b.info: 'Earth's cousin': a bigger, older Earth round a Sun-like star.
realweather.target.kepler10b.info: A rocky world so close to its star that its rock melts.
realweather.target.kepler78b.info: An Earth-sized lava world with a year of 8.5 hours.
realweather.target.kepler1649c.info: An Earth-sized world in its red dwarf's habitable zone.
realweather.target.kepler442b.info: One of the most Earth-like planets known.
realweather.target.kepler62f.info: A super-Earth that may be covered in ocean and ice.
realweather.target.trappist1b.info: The innermost of seven: scorched and maybe volcanic.
realweather.target.trappist1c.info: A rocky world, perhaps with a thick hot sky like Venus.
realweather.target.trappist1d.info: A small world at the inner edge of the habitable zone.
realweather.target.trappist1e.info: The most Earth-like of the seven, maybe with oceans.
realweather.target.trappist1f.info: A cool world, maybe an ocean under ice.
realweather.target.trappist1h.info: The outermost of seven: a frozen world.
realweather.target.gj1214b.info: A steamy 'water world' hidden under thick haze.
realweather.telescope.earth: You're standing on it! A telescope can't show it from here.
realweather.planet_map.title: Planet map: which world do you want to visit?
realweather.planet_map.hint: Drag to fly round (low down: to look about). Wheel, W/S or the buttons to go down and up. Esc to leave.
realweather.target.ton618.info: A quasar powered by one of the biggest black holes known: 66 billion times the Sun's mass. Zoom right in to see its shadow, photon ring, accretion disc and the light bent round it. A huge swarm of bright stars with planets circles it.
realweather.space.left_ozone: You have left the ozone layer: you are in space now
realweather.space.back_in_air: Back inside the air, under the ozone layer
realweather.space.earth_below: The whole Earth is below you
realweather.target.orion_nebula.info: The nearest great stellar nursery: glowing hydrogen and oxygen lit by the young Trapezium stars.
realweather.target.crab_nebula.info: What is left of the supernova seen in 1054: a net of glowing filaments round a pulsar.
realweather.target.eagle_nebula.info: Home of the Pillars of Creation: towers of dark dust where stars are being born.
realweather.target.lagoon_nebula.info: A huge pink cloud split by a dark lane, with a bright hourglass at its heart.
realweather.target.trifid_nebula.info: A red glow cut into three by dark lanes, with a blue reflection cloud above.
realweather.target.carina_nebula.info: One of the largest nebulae in the sky, round the giant star Eta Carinae.
realweather.target.ring_nebula.info: A glowing ring of gas blown off by a dying star, now a white dwarf at its centre.
realweather.target.helix_nebula.info: The 'Eye of God': a thick ring of gas round a white dwarf, close to us.
realweather.target.dumbbell_nebula.info: A planetary nebula shaped like an apple core, glowing green and red.
realweather.target.cats_eye_nebula.info: Nested shells and jets thrown off by a dying star.
realweather.target.eskimo_nebula.info: A bright inner bubble in a 'fur hood' of filaments.
realweather.target.horsehead_nebula.info: A dark horse's head of dust against a curtain of glowing red hydrogen.
realweather.target.flame_nebula.info: An orange glow torn by branching dark lanes, like a burning fire.
realweather.target.rosette_nebula.info: A rose of red gas hollowed out by the hot young stars at its centre.
Shaped like the continent, with the bright 'Cygnus Wall' along its 'Gulf of Mexico'.
realweather.target.veil_nebula.info: Delicate arcs of glowing filaments: the edge of an old supernova's blast.
realweather.target.tarantula_nebula.info: The brightest star-forming region we know, in the Large Magellanic Cloud, spidery filaments round the cluster R136.
realweather.target.omega_nebula.info: The 'Swan': a bright curved bar of glowing gas.
realweather.target.cone_nebula.info: A dark cone-shaped pillar of dust, under the Christmas Tree cluster.
realweather.target.bubble_nebula.info: A thin bubble of gas blown by the wind of one massive star.
realweather.target.california_nebula.inf: A long red cloud shaped like the state of California.
realweather.target.heart_nebula.info: A heart of glowing hydrogen round a cluster of young stars.
realweather.target.soul_nebula.info: The Heart's neighbour: a red cloud with two great hollows.
realweather.target.witch_head_nebula.inf: A blue cloud of dust lit by Rigel, in the profile of a witch's face.
realweather.target.running_man_nebula.in: A blue reflection nebula with the dark figure of a running man in it.
realweather.target.crab_pulsar.info: The neutron star at the heart of the Crab Nebula, spinning 30 times a second.
realweather.target.vela_pulsar.info: A young neutron star spinning 11 times a second, with its own wind nebula.
realweather.target.psr_b1919_21.info: The first pulsar ever found (1967): one pulse every 1.34 seconds.
realweather.target.psr_j1748_2446ad.info: The fastest spinning pulsar known: 716 turns a second, in the cluster Terzan 5.
realweather.target.psr_j0437_4715.info: The nearest bright millisecond pulsar, 174 turns a second, with a white dwarf partner.
realweather.travel.arrived: Welcome to %s! You can build here. Use the planet map to go home.
realweather.travel.orbit: In orbit above %s: you will drift slowly down to its ground.
realweather.cmd.space_graphics: Space graphics: %s (auto, low, medium, high, ultra or off)
realweather.travel.gas: You are falling into the clouds of %s. There is no ground: deeper down, the heat and pressure near its core will kill you.
realweather.travel.site: You are in deep space beside %s. Look where to go and use the movement keys to fly round it.
realweather.gas.sinking: Sinking through the clouds of %s: there is no surface to land on.
realweather.gas.heat: The heat and crushing pressure inside %s are burning you up!
death.attack.realweather.star: %1$s flew too close to a star and burned up
death.attack.realweather.black_hole: %1$s crossed a black hole's event horizon and was torn apart
death.attack.realweather.pulsar: %1$s was killed by a neutron star's radiation
death.attack.realweather.planet_core: %1$s sank too deep into a gas giant and was crushed by the heat of its core
item.realweather.light_drive.speed: Speed: %s%% of the speed of light
item.realweather.light_drive.on: Switched on: look up at a world and walk forward to fly to it
realweather.drive.no_route: The light drive flies only between the worlds of our solar system (use the planet map for other stars).
realweather.drive.launch: Leaving %s at %s%% of the speed of light!
realweather.drive.slider: Speed: %s%% of the speed of light
realweather.drive.speed: %s km per second: one astronomical unit in %s minutes
realweather.drive.help1: Hold it switched on, look up at a planet in the sky and walk forward: you take off and fly through space to it.
realweather.drive.help2: In space it sets how fast you fly (time runs 200x faster between the planets).
realweather.flight.between: Between the planets of the solar system
realweather.flight.drive: Light drive: %s%% of the speed of light (time x%s)
realweather.flight.drive_site: Light drive: %s%% of the speed of light
realweather.flight.thrusters: Thrusters only (hold the light drive, switched on, to go faster)
realweather.flight.hint: Look where to go: W forward, S back, A/D sideways, Space/Shift up/down. Get close to a world to land. Planet map: home.
realweather.flight.hint_site: Look where to go: W forward, S back, A/D sideways, Space/Shift up/down. Sprint for speed. Planet map: home.
realweather.target.io.info: Jupiter's volcanic moon: hundreds of active volcanoes, plumes of sulphur 300 km high.
realweather.target.europa.info: Jupiter's ice moon, an ocean hidden under its cracked shell of ice.
realweather.target.ganymede.info: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury.
realweather.target.callisto.info: Jupiter's old, dark moon, the most cratered world known.
realweather.target.titan.info: Saturn's moon with thick orange air, methane rain and lakes.
realweather.target.enceladus.info: Saturn's icy moon spraying jets of ice from the cracks at its south pole.
realweather.target.charon.info: Pluto's big moon, half its size, both always facing each other.
realweather.target.hiiaka.info: The larger moon of the dwarf planet Haumea.
realweather.target.namaka.info: The smaller, inner moon of Haumea.
realweather.target.dysnomia.info: The moon of the dwarf planet Eris.
realweather.target.triton.info: Neptune's moon going round it backwards, with geysers of nitrogen.
realweather.target.halley.info: The most famous comet, back every 76 years, with blue ion and yellow dust tails.
realweather.target.hale_bopp.info: The Great Comet of 1997: a huge nucleus and two brilliant tails.
realweather.target.neowise.info: The bright comet of 2020, its curved dust tail seen all over the world.
realweather.target.sgr_1806_20.info: A magnetar: the strongest magnetic field known. Its 2004 starquake flare lit Earth's upper air.
realweather.target.gw150914.info: Two black holes spiralling together, sending out gravitational waves: the first ever detected.
realweather.target.sn1987a.info: A star that exploded in 1987: its shock front races out and lights up the ring round it.
realweather.target.sgr_a_star.info: The black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, 4 million Suns, ringed by a swarm of stars racing round it.
realweather.target.m87_star.info: 6.5 billion Suns in the galaxy M87, photographed in 2019, shooting a jet 5000 light years long.
